paper.title: BEER: Fast O(1/T) Rate for Decentralized Nonconvex Optimization with Communication Compression

algorithm.name: BEER (Algorithm 1), full-gradient deterministic specialization
citations: PDF p.4 Assumption 2.1 and Eq.(2): symmetric doubly stochastic mixing W with positive spectral gap.
PDF p.5 Definition 2.2, Eq.(3): E||C(v)-v||^2 <= (1-alpha)||v||^2; biased compression is allowed.
PDF p.6 Section 3 matrix notation: X=[x1,...,xn] is d by n and compression applies independently to columns.
PDF p.7 Algorithm 1 line 1: common X0, H0=G0=0 and V0=grad F(X0).
PDF p.7 Algorithm 1 lines 3-5: descent using V and consensus using H, then compress Xnew-H and accumulate into H.
PDF p.7 Algorithm 1 lines 6-8: gradient tracking using old G consensus plus consecutive gradient difference, then compress Vnew-G and accumulate into G.
PDF p.7 Section 4.1: exact full gradients may replace stochastic minibatch gradients when local variance is zero.
assumptions: The allowed source is only the designated arXiv:2201.13320v3 PDF. Cases are independently derived finite trajectories; no implementation or prior evaluation output was consulted.

The deterministic diagonal quadratic objectives are smooth, bounded below, have a minimizer, and are a valid zero-variance specialization. They test the algorithmic recurrence, not nonconvex convergence rates or stochastic minibatch sampling.
Mixing matrices are symmetric, nonnegative, doubly stochastic, connected and have positive spectral gap: first case eigenvalues (1,0.5), second case (1,0.75,0.25).

Top1 in dimension two satisfies Definition 2.2 with alpha=1/2; scaling by 1/2 satisfies it with alpha=3/4. The scale case tests the mathematical compressor interface and makes no claim of actual communication savings.

The finite input step sizes are explicit; the paper convergence theorem contains unspecified absolute constants, so these three-round probes do not claim a theorem-certified learning-rate choice or eventual convergence.
Matrix and objective layouts, exact gradient formula, compressor tie rule, initialization, update order, observation timing and output names are fully specified in each public case.

The paper does not prescribe a generic software return object or stopping rule. After exactly three full rounds, observe all four algorithm states; no implicit averaging or random-iterate selection is used.

cases.purpose: Activate biased sparse communication, residual accumulation and support changes in both control sequences, and distinguish gradient tracking from plain local gradients after consensus starts.

compressor.name: top1
compressor.rule: Retain the original value at the coordinate of largest absolute value; set all other coordinates to zero. On an exact tie choose the lowest zero-based coordinate index. C(0)=0. No rescaling.

observation_semantics.state_layout: All observed X,H,V,G matrices have shape [dimension][number_of_clients]; columns index clients in the same order as W rows/columns. Objectives below use [client][dimension] arrays.
observation_semantics.step_semantics: Step 0 is immediately after Algorithm 1 initialization. Step t>=1 is after completing lines 3-8 for iteration t-1. Report exactly X,H,V,G at every requested step. Q_h,Q_g and averages are not requested observations.
observation_semantics.initialization: X^0 has every column equal to initial_common_point; H^0=G^0=zero matrices; V^0=the exact local gradient at each corresponding column of X^0.
observation_semantics.objective: Client i has f_i(x)=0.5*sum_j quadratic_diagonals_by_client[i][j]*(x[j]-quadratic_centers_by_client[i][j])^2. Gradient coordinate j is diagonal[i][j]*(x[j]-center[i][j]). Global f is (1/n)*sum_i f_i. No extra regularization, momentum, projection, clipping, or stochastic noise.
observation_semantics.update_order: Execute Algorithm 1: Xnew=X+gamma*H*(W-I)-eta*V; Qh=C(Xnew-H); Hnew=H+Qh; Vnew=V+gamma*G*(W-I)+gradF(Xnew)-gradF(X); Qg=C(Vnew-G); Gnew=G+Qg. Unsubscripted X,H,V,G on right sides denote pre-round values, except the explicitly named Xnew/Vnew.
observation_semantics.compression_scope: Invoke the same deterministic compressor independently on each client column of each residual matrix, for both the H and G channels. Do not compress globally across the matrix or compress the raw X/V in place of residuals.

cases.purpose: Exercise a different valid biased contractive map on both residual channels with a noncomplete graph, dimension unequal to client count, and client-specific anisotropic quadratic curvature.

compressor.name: scale
compressor.rule: For every residual vector v return C(v)=0.5*v, coordinatewise. This deterministic biased map satisfies Definition 2.2 with alpha=0.75; it is an algebraic compression-map test, not a claim of bit savings.
